text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Danish justice minister Frank Jensen is ready to ban the Hells Angels and Bandidos biker groups if Denmark's public procecuter rules that they have violence and crime as their sole purpose. The government has granted 38 million crowns to build four special biker cells in prisons.

--- Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) is targetting tourists and backpackers with cheap trips including hotel overnights at times when its aircraft fly half empty. The airline's office and ground staff at Copenhagen airport are threatening strike action in March if their demands for a new wage agreement are not met by management.

--- Shareholders have become 78 billion crowns richer since the beginning of 1997, a 15.7 percent rise in stock values, placing Copenhagen Stock Exchange among the five world bourses with the biggest share price rises this year.
--- Danish companies can expect a rise in exports due to increasing growth with more investment and new jobs in Germany.
